quotes.source_excerpt: "According to psychology, people who build fake scenarios in their heads while staring out windows are experiencing maladaptive daydreaming. It's a coping mechanism, the mind escaping into imagined worlds that feel safer than real life. It shows up everywhere—conversations you wish went differently, crafting the perfect comeback, future arguments, your favorite song that becomes the soundtrack for the moment you finally win or finally feel seen. This activates the brain's default mode network, triggering a dopamine release, the same rewards real success would give. But because it's imagined, the comfort is only temporary. Maladaptive daydreaming isn't a weakness; it's emotional regulation. But the danger is escaping becoming easier than living."
